## Summary

I'm a statistician, data scientist and AI engineer with more than ten years of experience, working mostly in R and Python. I started in climate and agricultural research, where I learned to build models that other people had to trust and act on. Since 2021 I've applied the same habits to industry problems: customer churn and segmentation, pricing, forecasting, recommendation and text embeddings, and more recently LLM-based agents.

I like the part of the job between the notebook and production: cleaning up the data, making the model reproducible, and getting it running somewhere useful (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Kubeflow, Docker).

## Experience

### AI Engineer · Globant, on assignment at Disney {.cv-role}
*Dec 2025 – Present · Remote, Colombia*

Building LLM-based systems for Disney:

- A multi-agent system that reads a codebase and generates its documentation, with structured context injection, schema validation between agents and a clear split between deterministic and LLM steps to make results reliable and explainable.
- A conversational intake agent that standardizes internal product requests, pushes back on vague input and flags overlap across teams.
- An automated reporting pipeline that gathers data from project-management tools into one reporting model and produces scheduled executive and team reports, with a dry-run step before anything is distributed.

Tools: Python, LangGraph, Azure OpenAI, REST APIs, Docker, Git, CI/CD.

### Senior Data Scientist · Globant {.cv-role}
*May 2021 – Dec 2025 · Remote, Colombia*

**Sportian account** (Aug 2023 – Dec 2025)

- Built statistical and machine learning models for sports-industry products, mainly pricing and match analytics.
- Worked with time series, econometric methods and embeddings on historical sales and event data.

**Augmented Staffing** (Feb 2022 – Jan 2023)

- Forecasting and clustering of internal staffing tickets, used to plan recruiting.
- Built a semantic search and recommendation tool that matched candidates to tickets using text embeddings, plus a seniority estimation model in PyTorch with an ordinal loss.
- Ran the pipelines on Kubeflow.

**DirecTV** (May 2021 – Dec 2021)

- Customer segmentation for the DirecTV GO subscriber base.
- Churn model that combined behavioural usage data with sentiment from text, plus an analysis of subscription pricing and a market basket analysis to guide retention campaigns.
- Pipelines on AWS SageMaker.

### Professor (part-time) · Universidad del Valle and Universidad Católica {.cv-role}
*Aug 2020 – Jun 2021*

Taught time series analysis and probability at Universidad del Valle, and inference and probability at Universidad Católica.

### Research Assistant and Data Scientist · CIAT (International Center for Tropical Agriculture) {.cv-role}
*2014 – 2020 · Cali, Colombia*

Climate and agriculture group. I automated, in R, the full pipeline from climate data to crop simulation, and modelled climate variables and crop yields across Latin America and beyond. Highlights:

- Impacts of near-term climate change on major crops in Latin America and the Caribbean (for the IDB and USAID), using DSSAT and ORYZA crop models together with machine learning and geostatistics.
- Identification of "climate service hotspots" worldwide, where agro-climatic information could help close yield gaps ([AgMetGaps](https://ciat-dapa.github.io/AgMetGaps/)).
- Statistical models behind the AClimate Colombia seasonal forecast platform ([paper](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.compag.2020.105486)).
- Regional climate change plan for the Orinoco region (Meta, Casanare, Vichada and Arauca): spatial analysis, climate clusters and yield simulation for the main production systems.
- Vulnerability analysis and classification of production systems for Colombia's Fondo Adaptación, with CORPOICA.

### Earlier work, 2010 – 2014 {.cv-role}

- **Consultant, Universidad del Valle** (2012–2013): statistical design and analysis for two engineering theses, one on constructed wetlands (factorial and repeated-measures designs, mixed models) and one on equations of state (non-linear models, bootstrap).
- **Professor, Universidad Santiago de Cali** (2013): a course on statistics in R for research faculty.
- **Statistical Assistant, Universidad del Valle** (2010–2013): analysis for the quality and accreditation office of the health faculty, with Excel macros and R automation.

## Education
